hook_text: How did a new way of drawing, a printing machine and a lot of curiosity help send ships around Africa?
clip_script: Makhanda, an art lesson. Two lines meet at a point on the horizon, and suddenly the road looks real. Renaissance artists in Italy used this trick, called perspective. The Renaissance, meaning rebirth, began in Italy and spread across Europe in the 1400s and 1500s. People studied old Greek and Roman books, asked new questions, tested ideas and printed books on Gutenberg's press. New ideas spread fast. A turning point in Europe, and a push towards exploration.
visual_style: Whiteboard road drawn in perspective, then a printing press stamping pages, then ships setting out from a harbour.
mood: Bright and inspiring, like the lights coming on in a dark room.
pacing: Quick drawing trick first, steady explanation of new ideas, ending on ships leaving harbour.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a road or railway line using perspective.
